title: "Shepherd and Shepherdess" fan and case
medium: Paper, mother-of-pearl, glass jewel, copper alloy rivet; opaque watercolor, watercolor, gold paint, and gold paper trim, carved and incised sticks and guards with applied silver gilt and gold foil, rivet
medium_parts: Paper, mother-of-pearl, glass jewel, copper alloy rivet

identifying_description: Leaf of paper with opaque watercolor, watercolor, gold paint, and gold paper trim, showing at center a couple conversing before a classical ruin, a seated woman and young girl with pinwheel at left, and a shepherd attending two sheep at right. On the reverse shows a floral border. Sticks and guards of carved and incised mother-of-pearl with applied silver gilt and gold foil. Glass jewel and copper alloy rivet
web_text: Idyllic countrysides frequently served as backdrops in eighteenth-century fan designs, reflecting urban society's idealization of the pastoral. This interest is further heightened by this fan's illustration of several elegantly dressed shepherds and shepherdesses in the foreground. In the center, one shepherdess has discarded her houlette (sheephook) for an amorous interlude, resting against a ruined column with her paramour. Depictions of ancient ruins appear frequently in fans made during the second half of the eighteenth century, after the rediscovery of the ancient cities of Herculaneum (1709) and Pompeii (1748).
